AlternateTargets: the five positions of the Caodong house
Senses.Explanation: The Caodong Five Ranks are a named five-part scheme associated with Dongshan Liangjie and Caoshan Benji. Corpus passages identify sets framed through upright and crooked, ruler and minister, merit, princes, or facing the guest; later records repeatedly pair the Five Ranks with the Linji house's Three Mysteries when distinguishing house vocabularies. Questions can ask for the ranks as a whole or for each member in order. The headword names the fivefold scheme, while the particular paired terms specify its formulation.
Senses.Note: The frozen corpus has 1,279 exact hits in 233 files representing 230 works. The technical anchors include defining enumerations, verses, house comparisons, interview questions, and later summaries. In the Caoshan facing-the-guest cases, the unnamed monk—not Caoshan—utters the headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師。作五位君臣頌云。正中偏。三更初夜月明前。莫怪相逢不相識。隱隱猶懷舊日嫌。偏中正。失曉老婆逢古鏡。分明覿面別無真。休更迷頭猶認影。正中來。無中有路隔塵埃。但能不觸當今諱。也勝前朝斷舌才。兼中至。兩刃交鋒不須避。好手猶如火裏蓮。宛然自有冲天志。兼中到。不落有無誰敢和。人人盡欲出常流。折合還歸炭裏坐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dongshan Liangjie of Ruizhou (瑞州洞山良价禪師語錄) records Dongshan Liangjie composing the ruler-and-minister Five Ranks verses and naming all five positions in order.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因有僧問五位君臣旨訣。師曰。正位即空界。本來無物。偏位即色界。有萬象形。正中偏者背理就事。偏中正者舍事入理。兼帶者冥應眾緣。不墮諸有。非染非淨。非正非偏。故曰虛玄大道無著真宗。從上先德推此一位最妙最玄。當詳審辨明。君為正位。臣為偏位。臣向君是偏中正。君視臣是正中偏。君臣道合是兼帶語。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Caoshan Yuanzheng of Fuzhou (撫州曹山元證禪師語錄) records Caoshan Benji defining the upright and crooked positions, their combinations, and the ruler-and-minister mapping.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示以偏正五位。四賓主功勳五位。君臣五位。王子五位。內外紹等事。偏正五位者。正中偏者。體起用也。偏中正者。用歸體也。兼中至。體用並至也。兼中到。體用俱泯也。四賓主。不同臨濟。主中賓。體中用也。賓中主。用中體也。賓中賓。用中用。頭上安頭也。主中主。物我雙忘。人法俱泯。不涉正偏位也。功勳五位者。明參學功位至於非功位也。君臣五位者。明有為無為也。王子五位者。明內紹本自圓成。外紹有終有始也。大約曹洞家風。不過體用偏正賓主。以明向上一路。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Eyes of Humans and Gods (人天眼目), compiled by Huiyan Zhizhao, explains the upright-and-crooked, merit, ruler-and-minister, and prince Five Ranks and relates the positions to substance, function, succession, and the Caodong house style.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不是臨濟三玄不是曹洞五位不是入理深談不是門庭施設
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Foguo (佛國禪師語錄), Foguo rejects identification with Linji's three mysteries, Caodong's Five Ranks, deep talk entering principle, or institutional devices.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是洞上五位？」荅：「除夜舊門神。」君義臣忠，父慈子孝，要嫁竹夫人，土地前討笤，報道石幢子，生來多不肖。且道侍奉一句又作麼生？若還借借終不玅。問：「如何是三要？」荅：「棺材屋裏掛鍾馗。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Mingyu (三宜盂禪師語錄), an unnamed monk asks what the Dongshan-school Five Ranks are; Sanyi Mingyu answers ‘old door-gods on New Year's Eve’ without repeating the headword, and later answers a separate question about the three essentials. All six attribution rungs leave the questioner personally unnamed.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 張旦公居士問 explicitly makes Layman Zhang Dangong the named non-master subject of the headword-bearing question; Yunxi Langting supplies the answer.

Senses.Explanation: Five positions is also an ordinary count phrase for a five-member sequence not referring to the Caodong scheme. Context identifies the particular series, such as successive positions in an explanatory classification or an ordinal place. This sense is retained to prevent every standalone occurrence from being forced into the house-specific reading.
Senses.Note: This sense denotes five-member sequences other than the named Caodong Five Ranks. Its three exact anchors come from two independent works: the Patriarchs' Hall Collection (work:B25n0144) and Yongming Yanshou's Source-Mirror Record (work:T48n2016); the two Yanshou rows count once.
